ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Hong Kong: Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Ordinance (Cap. 615) (AMLO), Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622) Part 7A on Significant Controllers Register, and Limited Partnership Ordinance (Cap. 37). Mainland China: Measures for the Administration of Corporate Beneficial Owner Information issued by PBOC and SAMR (Order No. 3, effective 1 November 2024), applicable to PRC-origin beneficial ownership records.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the Hong Kong SAR gazetted authentication authority; no consular legalization of the Hong Kong Companies Registry certificate shall be sought while the Apostille Convention applies

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Current Status Certificate
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Hong Kong Companies Registry / Business Registration Office of the Inland Revenue Department
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille only; reciprocal consular legalization is excluded as Hong Kong SAR is within an Apostille Contracting Party framework

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of China or its authorized provincial foreign affairs office; no additional consular legalization after apostille

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All proposed partners, general partners, ultimate beneficial owners, exercise of control persons, and authorized signatories must undergo continuous screening against the OFAC SDN List, the UN Security Council Consolidated List, the UK HM Treasury Consolidated List, the EU consolidated sanctions list, and domestic screens under AMLO and the United Nations Sanctions Ordinance. Enhanced due diligence must investigate PEP status of politically exposed persons, family members, close associates, adverse media, adverse sanctions designations, and source of wealth for any beneficial owner holding 25% or more of the partnership. Screening must be documented in a timestamped compliance report and re-run at onboarding and at any trigger event including changes in ownership or sanctions updates.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Hong Kong Companies Registry - ICRIS Electronic Name Search and Reservation Portal (www.icris.cr.gov.hk)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A foreign-invested partnership in Hong Kong may adopt an English name and, optionally, a Chinese commercial name in traditional Chinese characters. The English name must not be identical or too similar to an existing name on the Companies Register; no phonetic or transliterated four-tier naming structure is mandated. The Chinese name, if used, must correspond to the English name for transliteration purposes and must not create misleading equivalence with a prohibited tainted token.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Limited liability marker confusion such as Limited, Corporation, Incorporated, Public Limited Company, Open-ended Fund Company without lawful authorization
Words indicating sovereign status, banking, insurance, trust, securities, deposit-taking, exchange, clearing or similar regulated activity
Tokens implying falsely a connection to the government, the People's Liberation Army, central bank, or consular authorities
Offensive, obscene, seditious, or contrary to public order expressions under the Companies Ordinance and Chinese common law prohibitions
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Companies Registry rejects a name application, the applicant must first obtain the written rejection notice identifying the conflicting or prohibited token. Within 21 days of the notice, the applicant may file a formal appeal with the Companies Registry's Name Committee or the Review Board under the Companies Ordinance, attaching proof of prior use, user-in-trade reputation, consent from the defective entity where applicable, and a proposed compromise name. If the Registrar still maintains the refusal, the applicant may seek judicial review in the Court of First Instance within 60 days, but must do so only after exhausting the administrative appeal and without commencing a new business under the contested name.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox is not permissible for the aircraft rotables distribution industry as the Hong Kong Companies Registrar, the Inland Revenue Department, and banks require a physical registered office in Hong Kong capable of receiving service of process and retaining the Significant Controllers Register and AML records. A private mailbox provider that does not offer physical reception, document storage, in-person compliance oversight, and director or partner attendance facilities will be rejected for business registration and will fail bank account opening, escrow due diligence, and trade licensing processes.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (1) verify front-door signage and company name plate; (2) confirm reception and secure filing areas contain the Significant Controllers Register, partnership records, and business registration certificates; (3) ensure a responsible officer can attend within 15 minutes for unannounced inspection by the Companies Registry, IRD, Customs and Excise Department, and the Hong Kong Police Financial Investigation Division. Quantified risk: High (60-70% probability) for trading companies in regulated aviation spares with cross-border escrow payments, based on municipal registration and tax suppression statistics.
